concept: Branch Lines with only its type re-set, as one IBM Plex superfamily whose width is the hierarchy. Everything the signal box's panel is engraved with (titles, heads, labels, the timetables' stamps, counts, the keys and the bar) is Plex Sans Condensed; everything the family keeps and says (rows, words, fields, the ways to start) is Plex Sans; Plex Mono prints only the machine's own name and small print, and the tubes stay VT323. Zero is dotted everywhere, and every lamp, ring and prompt hangs outside the words' edge. It should feel like the same calm signal box at night, its legends engraved in one engineering hand.
companions: Unchanged from the parent, by the roll: steel-cyan #a7c4d8 for the family's hand and the wiring (rails, rings, links, the backlit steel key for here), green-black slate boards and plates, section and kind colours only in rings and lamps, amber only for late and needs a look, and #6dff9c only for now and live (the mark, 'next', Send, the box, the now lamps and runs, her screens, the tubes).
title: What’s *next* for us? (the parent's words, kept by a dice mutant), now set at the title step in the condensed face.
decisions: The face: of the three condensed faces the dice offered, IBM Plex Sans Condensed. Barlow Condensed is the highway-sign face the panel faded as sporty 'trail-sign' heads (round 6) and has no stylistic sets; Archivo narrow was already the parent's title face at 84%, its 400 body is pale (round 12) and it has no stylistic sets either. Plex Condensed pairs with Plex Sans and Plex Mono as one superfamily (rewarded in rounds 6, 8 and 12: condensed Plex heads over Plex body), is IBM's own hand for an IBM-green screen, and carries the sets the third roll needs.

The system: width is the hierarchy. Condensed for what the panel is engraved with (page titles, section heads, the 14px label step, stamps and relative days, counts and figures, the chat's speaker names and times, field labels, the bar, tabs, keys and buttons); Plex Sans for what the family keeps and says (row names, Vera's and the family's words, ledes, help, fields and the select's words, the ways to start); Plex Mono only for the wordmark, the footer's small print and code; VT323 unchanged on the glass.

The stamps left the typewriter: every date, time and relative day that the parent set in DM Mono is now a condensed legend in Plex's own tabular lining figures (Plex's digits are tabular by default, so the timetable margins, the chat's spine, To do's Due column and the Drive column still read straight down). This answers round 13's 'whole phrases in letterspaced mono were not rewarded' and the revival judge's 'set the date kicker in condensed'.

The scale, written: title 48.8px/600 at -0.008em, head 24px/600, legend 14px/500 at +0.01em, keys and the bar 16px condensed (500; 600 on the primary), body 16/1.6 Plex Sans 400 with row names at 600, small text 14px. Figures: the page figure 400 in the label's steel, the fortnight's day numerals 34px/600, the tally 42px/600. The heads' extra word-spacing came down from .08em to .03em, since Plex Condensed's space is already open; the smallest words rise from 11.52px to 12px (the phone's fortnight 'in 4 days' from 11.5 to 13px).

Home's question is the page's title, so it is set at the title step in the condensed face: clamp(1.875rem, 4.4vw, 3.05rem), 48.8px on the desktop and 30px on a phone. At 34px it broke to two lines on the phone, so the floor was stepped down until it held one.

The stylistic set: ss04, Plex's dotted zero, in the Sans and the Condensed, the zero Plex Mono draws by default, so zero is drawn one way on the whole page off the glass (the lineage was faulted for drawing it two ways). ss01 and ss02 (the simple a and g) were left off: the panel found Plex's schoolbook a and g soft in round 10. Every font shorthand resets the features, so the set is held at * with !important and the mono is given its own back.

Hung by hand: the Next up tube's '>' prompt hangs in the glass's margin, so '4 more on the radar' stands on the title's edge; Lately added's and the kids' rings stand under the head's icon with the names on the head's own words (they were 4.8px in); Status's bands likewise; the Ideas and Settings lists' names stand on the page title's edge, their rings and icons hanging to its left (they were 3-4px in); Coming up's note starts on the head's words; the numbered steps and the tips list on the settings pages hang their numerals and bullets outside the paragraph; To do's column heads now stand on their columns (Who was 2px off).

The one markup change: ideas.html's drive macro pads the minutes to two digits ('2 h 05 min'), so the Drive column's tabular figures line up, as the type judge asked. On the glass, .rel now inherits the tube's VT323, so the Ideas tube's '18 min NW' is the tube's own letter again.

Nothing else moved: the colours, the light, the layout, the lines and the words are the parent's. The sources are the parent's, re-set by src/retype.py (each replacement must match once) plus src/type.css, built by src/build.py to 58.4K of 60K.
strengths: One rule that holds on every page, Plans, To do and Settings included: the panel's legends are condensed, the family's words are in the text face, and the change is in every line of every page.
The timetables read as engraved legends rather than typewriter phrases, and every figure is tabular, so the margins, the Drive column and Status's tables align without a monospace.
Zero is drawn one way, dotted, across the page, which gives the figures a quiet machine texture (10:00, $0.00, 30 September).
The question is now the largest head on Home, at the title step, and holds one line on a phone.
Markers hang: each list's names stand on its head's words or the page title's edge, with rings, lamps and the tube's prompt in the margin.
0 targets under 44px on every rendered page, no sideways scroll, smallest words 12px (from 11.52).
weaknesses: It is a type mutant: 3-9% of the pixels differ from the parent (Home 8.3%, Chat 4.2%, Status 2.7%). At half size it reads as Branch Lines, and the parent's colour faults carry over unchanged (Chat 97% and Status 99% green by share).
Plex has only tabular figures, so in running text a 1 takes a whole figure's width with its slab foot: '$1.26' and '10:00' look gappy in prose.
The dotted zero also reaches Vera's own words ('10:00 to 14:00'), where some will find it fussy or machine-like.
The set is held with a universal !important, the blunt tool the round-13 type judge disliked.
Condensed and text face are one design, so the contrast between a legend and a row is a width, not a voice. DM Sans' round warmth is gone, and Plex SemiBold row names are denser.
Checkbox labels that are whole sentences (Memory's 'A must or a never (an allergy, a rule), not only a taste') read tight in the condensed face.
The quote half of the roll has nothing to hang: no rendered page starts a line with a quotation mark (the only quotes sit mid-line on Status and Memory), so no quote rule was written.
The tube's hung prompt sits about 5px from the glass's edge, and Plex Sans Condensed is served as static weights, so the parent's 650 heads became 600.
measures: ink_on_bg 12.75, brand_on_bg 15.18 (both the parent's); green share Home 79.8%, Ideas 84.8%, Chat 97.3%, Status 99.1%; hue entropy .38/.35/.29/.25; 0 of 57 Home targets under 44px (0 on every page); smallest words 12px; no sideways scroll; css 58.4K of 60K; one guideline flag, Ideas' words 28.3% different, inherited from the parent.
